question: How do people train a long-context Transformer model over 32K context length using sequence parallelism techniques? How are these methods compared with each other?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains sequence parallelism as distributing the computation of a long input sequence across multiple devices/accelerators, sharding the sequence dimension so per-device memory and compute drop, enabling 32K+ context training without changing the model architecture.
examples: Sequence parallelism splits the sequence dimension across GPUs so each device handles only a shard of tokens
By distributing computation, memory and compute per device drop, enabling long-context training with unchanged model architecture

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes Ring Attention as blockwise computation of self-attention and feedforward across devices in a ring topology, with key-value blocks rotated between devices while communication is fully overlapped with blockwise attention computation, achieving exact results without approximation or added communication/computation overhead.
examples: Devices hold shards of the sequence and pass KV blocks around the ring, fully hiding communication
Ring Attention trains long contexts exactly, without approximations or extra communication overhead, enabling contexts up to device-count times longer

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer presents DistFlashAttention as a distributed, memory-efficient attention extending FlashAttention to multi-GPU long-context training with three key techniques: token-level workload balancing, overlapping key-value communication, and rematerialization-aware gradient checkpointing.
examples: DistFlashAttention cuts quadratic peak memory to linear by combining FlashAttention with three distributed techniques
Its contributions are token-level workload balancing, overlapped KV communication, and rematerialization-aware checkpointing

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains Striped Attention as a simple extension of Ring Attention that fixes the workload imbalance caused by causal attention's triangular structure, assigning each device tokens distributed uniformly across the sequence instead of contiguous chunks.
examples: Causal attention's triangular structure causes imbalance in Ring Attention; Striped Attention gives each device a uniform strided subset of tokens
Each device holds non-contiguous tokens spread uniformly through the sequence, yielding even workloads

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer compares methods with concrete speedup/throughput numbers: DistFlashAttention's 4.45-5.64x over Ring Self-Attention, 1.24-2.01x over Megatron-LM with FlashAttention, 1.67x over Ring Attention, and 1.26-1.88x over DeepSpeed-Ulysses; plus Striped Attention's up to 1.45x end-to-end throughput over Ring Attention at 256K and 1.65x on 16 TPUv4 chips at 786K.
examples: DistFlashAttention achieves 4.45-5.64x speedup over Ring Self-Attention and 1.26-1.88x over DeepSpeed-Ulysses
Striped Attentention reaches 1.65x speedup at 786K sequence length on 16 TPUv4 chips

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: The answer reports achieved context lengths: DistFlashAttention evaluated on Llama-7B variants from 32K to 512K sequences, achieving 8x longer sequences than Ring Self-Attention and 2-8x longer than Megatron-LM; Ring Attention supports up to device-count times longer contexts and demonstrates million-token sequences.
examples: DistFlashAttention was evaluated on Llama-7B with sequence lengths 32K to 512K, achieving 8x longer sequences than Ring Self-Attention
Ring Attention demonstrates training with contexts of millions of tokens

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer mentions DeepSpeed-Ulysses as an alternative sequence-parallelism method using efficient all-to-all collective communication for attention computation, positioned as a baseline that DistFlashAttention outperforms by 1.26-1.88x.
examples: DeepSpeed-Ulysses employs all-to-all communication for sequence-parallel attention
DistFlashAttention achieves 1.26-1.88x speedup over DeepSpeed-Ulysses

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer synthesizes workload imbalance and its remedies as a common design concern across methods: triangular causal structure motivating Striped Attention's striping, and DistFlashAttention solving it at token-level granularity.
examples: Both Striped Attention's striping and DistFlashAttention's token-level workload balancing address uneven per-device attention workloads
Imbalance from causal masking motivated Striped Attention; DistFlashAttention resolves it at token granularity

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer synthesizes the relationships among methods: early ring-based approaches with imbalance issues, refinements (Striped Attention, DistFlashAttention) addressing load balance and memory, and overlapped KV communication as a shared key design idea.
examples: Both Ring Attention and DistFlashAttention overlap KV communication with attention computation
The lineage runs from Ring Attention's ring topology to Striped Attention's balancing and DistFlashAttention's token-level balancing plus memory optimizations

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer includes concrete evaluation details such as Llama-7B models and A100 GPUs for DistFlashAttention, and A100s/TPUv4s for Striped Attention.
examples: DistFlashAttention was evaluated on Llama-7B with sequences 32K-512K
Striped Attention was tested on A100s and TPUv4s, reaching 1.65x speedup at 786k on 16 TPUv4 chips
